basis: Acute myeloid leukemia is a malignant disorder of myeloid blood cells and bone marrow.
Substance-use disorder; intrinsic lasting organ damage is not established by this diagnosis.
Inherited early-onset immune dysregulation; supplied evidence does not establish additional organ damage in at least 30%.
Biotin deficiency commonly causes dermatitis/alopecia and neurologic dysfunction in untreated disease; frequencies are poorly quantified but plausibly exceed 30%.
Defined by neurodevelopmental impairment and corpus callosum abnormalities.
ABCA4-related retinal degeneration causes cone and rod dysfunction and progressive visual loss.
Malignant cutaneous sweat gland tumor.
Congenital nasal malformation; nose belongs to the pulmonary axis. Associated ocular and other structural defects are uncommon.
Fetal parvovirus infects erythroid precursors; anemia and thrombocytopenia occur in 80–99%. Cardiomyopathy and ocular abnormalities are below 30%.
Congenital hip dysplasia with joint deformity and subsequent hip osteoarthritis.
Hearing and visual impairment each affect 9/11; muscle atrophy affects 8/11. Respiratory failure reflects neuromuscular dysfunction rather than direct lung injury.
Malignant smooth muscle tumor originating in the kidney; smooth muscle histology does not imply skeletal muscle disease.
Clonal mast cell disorder with immune mediator activation; episodic flushing, gastrointestinal symptoms and hypotension do not establish lasting organ injury.
Malignancy originating in the gallbladder, which belongs to the hepatic axis.
Macular coloboma, juvenile nephronophthisis and mesomelic skeletal dysplasia with radiohumeral fusion define the syndrome.
Bone fragility defines disease; dentinogenesis imperfecta affects roughly 30–50%, and hearing loss roughly 30–50% over adulthood. Blue sclera alone is non-damaging.
Interferonopathy with destructive CNS disease; thrombocytopenia occurs in 2/5. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver injury; steatosis is 1/5.
Granulomatous prostatitis includes infectious and immune-mediated inflammation. The prostate itself lies outside the organ axes.
Umbrella of inherited phenylalanine and tyrosine metabolic disorders; additional organ damage is not consistently shared across subtypes.
MERTK-related retinal degeneration causes rod-cone dysfunction and progressive visual loss.
Intellectual and developmental impairment define disease; fifth-finger contractures affect 5/9 and toe syndactyly 3/9. Isolated 1/1 reports do not establish cohort prevalence.
PDA occurs in 7/19 (~37%); metopic synostosis in 3/3 and unilateral renal agenesis in 1/3 support structural involvement, with small denominators. Hearing loss is 4/16.
Inherited D-lactate metabolism defect; urinary lactate does not indicate renal injury. Frequencies of neurologic and ocular abnormalities are unestablished; gout is separate.
Isolated congenital absence or underdevelopment of breast tissue and nipples; breast has no axis.
Congenital urethral malformation defines disease; pelvic girdle bone abnormalities are frequent (30–79%). Urethra and associated reflux are within the renal axis.
